plain.li: [faith:devout] I'll tell it the way it was told to me, when I was small and the nights were long.
[faith:devout] This is how we try to live, and why.
[faith:devout] Ask me anything, the harder the better.
[faith:devout] When things were at their worst, this is what I held on to.
[faith:devout] There's a story about the first of us to walk this road.
[faith:devout,lowtech] My grandmother said these words over every harvest, and now I'll say them.
[faith:devout,!lowtech] Some of it's written down, but most you learn by living it.
[!faith:devout] I always wondered why you do that.
[!faith:devout] Mine says something like that too, in other words.
[!faith:devout] Can I ask something without it sounding rude?
[!faith:devout] Wait, go back a bit.
[faith:wavering] I used to be as sure of mine as you are of yours.

warm.li: [faith:devout] Thank you for coming, all of you.

blunt.li: [!faith:devout] I came for the warm seat, but the talk's not bad.

gloomy.li: [faith:devout] I've lost nearly everything once already, but never this.

cold.li: [!faith:devout] It hangs together better than I expected.

plain.li: My faith doesn't hold with being preached at, so I'll stay away.
I'll leave {FAITH} to those who hold it.
[faith:devout] We don't sit through other people's sermons, but it's nothing personal.
They can have their evening, I know what I believe.

gloomy.li: Every faith wants one more believer, and it won't be me.

cold.li: I don't need two hours of being told what to think.

plain.li: [poor] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, but the words wouldn't come right, and one by one the listeners found reasons to leave.
[poor] The evening of {FAITH} came to very little. {PAWN_nameDef} lost the thread halfway and never found it again.
[poor,believers] Only the faithful came to hear {PAWN_nameDef}, and they had heard it all before.
[good] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, plainly and without hurry, and answered every question put to {PAWN_objective}.
[good] An evening of {FAITH}: {PAWN_nameDef} told the old stories, and the listeners stayed to the end.
[good,altar] By the {PLACE}, {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, and for once nobody was watching the door.
[good,believers] The faithful of {FAITH} sat together while {PAWN_nameDef} spoke, and went to bed steadier for it.
[good,guide] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH} as its moral guide, and spoke well.
[fine] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, and the talk went on long after, in twos and threes, about what it means to believe anything.
[fine,!believers] Those who came to hear {PAWN_nameDef} speak for {FAITH} stayed late, even the doubters.
[fine,believers] The faithful of {FAITH} heard {PAWN_nameDef} out to the last word, and sat on together long after.
[fine,altar] At the {PLACE}, {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH} as if to each of them alone. It was very still afterwards.
[fine,moved] {PAWN_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH}, and some of those of other faiths left with a great deal to think about.
[speaker,poor] Spoke for {FAITH} tonight and made a mess of it. I'll do better next time.
[speaker,good] They listened to me tonight, and some stayed behind with questions about {FAITH}.
[speaker,fine] Tonight I spoke for {FAITH} and every word came out right. I'm still too awake to sleep.
[listener,unmoved] Went to hear {OTHER_nameDef} speak for {FAITH}. I see why it matters to {OTHER_objective}. It isn't mine.
[listener,poor] {OTHER_nameDef} tried to speak for {FAITH}. It didn't go well, and I felt for {OTHER_objective}.
[listener,moved] {OTHER_nameDef} spoke for {FAITH} tonight. I keep going over what was said.
[listener,fine,moved] I went to {OTHER_nameDef}'s evening out of curiosity and came back with more questions about my own faith than I took.

blunt.li: [listener,unmoved] {FAITH} evening. Long. The chairs were hard.

plain.li: [faith:devout] Ours after supper, theirs at first light, and that's fair.
[faith:devout] We'll leave it tidy for them, the way we'd want it left for us.
[!faith:devout] I'd never heard their words said out loud before.
[!faith:devout] Two faiths and one altar, but we'll manage.
[!faith:devout] It's strange, hearing someone else's words in this place.

blunt.li: [!faith:devout] As long as nobody sits in my seat.

plain.li: The council has named {FAITH} the colony's ideoligion. I'll keep mine all the same, quietly if I have to.
So {FAITH} is the colony's ideoligion now. Nobody asked me, and I won't forget that.
[faith:alone] One ideoligion for the colony, and I'm the only one left holding mine.

gloomy.li: The council chose one faith for the whole colony, and it isn't mine. I've never felt more like a guest here.

cold.li: {FAITH} is the colony's ideoligion by the council's word. Noted.

plain.li: [faith:devout] From today our faith is the colony's, and we'll carry it gently.
[faith:devout] You needn't believe a thing, but the door is open.
[!faith:devout] So that's that, then.
[!faith:devout] I'll believe what I believe, whatever the council says.
[!faith:devout] Does this change who does the cooking?

warm.li: [faith:devout] Whatever you hold to, you're still one of us.

gloomy.li: [!faith:devout] One faith for everyone never ends well in the stories.

plain.li: Before we start: a word from {FAITH}, as the council asked.
Let's begin as {FAITH} teaches, with a moment's quiet.
[faith:devout] A blessing on this meeting, in the way of {FAITH}. Now, to business.
May we choose well today. {FAITH} asks no more of us than that.

cheerful.li: A word from {FAITH} first, and I promise it's a short one.

cold.li: Say only what you mean today, as {FAITH} asks of us.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} reminds the council that today is {NAME}, and the evening belongs to {SUBJECT}.
[first] It's the first {NAME}, and those of {SUBJECT} have the chairs out already.
[years] {YEARS} years on, {NAME} comes round again, and {SUBJECT} keeps its evening.
[tradition] As every year, {NAME} is the evening of {SUBJECT}, and anyone may come.

gloomy.li: It's {NAME}. {A_nameDef} says a hard year is when the colony needs its evenings most.

plain.li: Today is {NAME}, the evening of {SUBJECT}. I mean to sit at the back and listen.
[first] The first {NAME}. We'll see if it lasts.
[tradition] It's {NAME} again. The same words every year, and I find I like that.
[faith:devout] It's {NAME}, and tonight the faith gets its evening, as it should every year.

blunt.li: Long evening ahead for {NAME}. Good company, at least.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} talked about what {SUBJECT} asks of a person.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} what {B_pronoun} believed in, and why.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} the story {A_pronoun} always tells on {NAME}.
[way:faith] {A_nameDef} reminded {B_nameDef} about tomorrow's ideoligion evening.
